### The Big Three

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](media/icecube/bert-ernie.png){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 410px;" fig-alt="IceCube event displays of Bert at left and Ernie at right, showing coloured optical-module hits from PeV cascades."}

::: {.media-caption}
**Bert and Ernie:** deposited energies $1.04\pm0.16$ and $1.14\pm0.17\,\mathrm{PeV}$.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="36%"}
![](media/icecube/big-bird.jpg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 410px;" fig-alt="IceCube's Big Bird cascade event display, with a bright central cluster of optical-module hits."}

::: {.media-caption}
**Big Bird:** approximately $2\,\mathrm{PeV}$ deposited.
:::
:::
:::::

::: {.takeaway}
What looks like a handful of coloured dots can reveal a cosmic particle shower.
:::

::: {.media-caption}
Event displays: IceCube Collaboration / IceCube–NSF.
[First two PeV events (2013)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.5356);
[three-year analysis (2014)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.5303).
:::

::: {.notes}
**0–3 minutes, including the title.** Start with the recognition tab. The prize
is a timely reason to look at the field, but this is a story of many people
and several complementary experiments. The portrait is the original image
embedded in DN's Stony Brook 2020 and HyperWebinar 2021 lectures.
It is not a photograph of the 2026 award ceremony.

Switch to the telescope. Most of the instrument is invisible in this picture:
its light sensors are frozen into the ice. We now know that a cosmic flux
exists. Its dominant sources and their internal physics remain the questions
that drive the field. Before discussing the measurements, ask how this
unusual idea became experimentally possible.

The Big Three tab shows iconic contained cascades. The quoted quantities
are deposited energies, not uniquely determined parent-neutrino energies.
Bert and Ernie were reported in 2013; Big Bird appeared in the 2014 three-year
analysis. The astrophysical-flux conclusion uses the event population and
background tests, rather than these displays alone. Use this optional tab
as a brief visual introduction to the measurement, preserving the opening's
three-minute allocation.
:::
